story.title: Civilians Evacuated from Oleshky Return to Ukraine Following Ceasefire
story.summary: Residents of the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated back to Ukraine after a ceasefire was brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. The civilians traveled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus to reach their homeland. Many evacuees were reunited with family members after years of being trapped in the occupied territory.

timeline_highlights.title: Russian Strikes Cause Casualties and Fires in Kyiv and Kharkiv
timeline_highlights.summary: Recent Russian missile and drone strikes in Ukraine have resulted in casualties and significant damage. In Kyiv, one person was killed and 15 injured, with emergency workers rescuing a dog from the rubble of damaged university buildings and a major bridge. Meanwhile, a drone strike in Kharkiv injured five people, including a 4-year-old child, and ignited several fires, prompting firefighters to respond amid ongoing threats of further attacks.

timeline_highlights.title: Russian Drone Strike on Dnipro Train Station Kills at Least 14
timeline_highlights.summary: A Russian drone attack on a crowded train station in Dnipro, Ukraine, resulted in at least 14 fatalities and numerous injuries, including an 11-year-old boy. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the incident as a 'horrific' attack, emphasizing the need for a response from Ukraine's allies. The strike occurred despite a local cease-fire in other areas, highlighting the ongoing violence in the region.

The attack injured several others, including an 11-year-old boy.

event_overview.title: About Sudan Conflict
event_overview.subject: Sudan Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Sudan conflict is an ongoing armed struggle that began on 15 April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), led by Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo. What began with fighting in and around Khartoum rapidly spread across Sudan, including Darfur and Kordofan, causing a nationwide humanitarian and displacement crisis and extensive damage to civilian infrastructure.

facts.label: Start date and principal parties
facts.value: Armed hostilities began on 15 April 2023 between the SAF and the RSF; the conflict followed a power struggle and disagreements linked to security-sector reform and the proposed integration of the RSF into the regular armed forces.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The conflict began in Khartoum and Merowe and quickly engulfed Darfur; it has since affected much of Sudan, with Khartoum, Darfur and Kordofan among the principal conflict-affected regions.

facts.label: Political context
facts.value: The war interrupted efforts to restore a civilian-led transition after Sudan's October 2021 military coup, following the 2019 overthrow of former president Omar al-Bashir.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: UN agencies describe the conflict as driving mass internal and cross-border displacement, acute hunger, and severely constrained access to essential services such as water, health care and shelter.

facts.label: Conduct of hostilities and civilian prot
facts.value: UN human-rights reporting has documented allegations of indiscriminate attacks in populated areas, including attacks involving airstrikes, shelling and explosive weapons, as well as other serious violations affecting civilians.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows chosen developments, including reported effects on electricity infrastructure, rather than providing a complete record of Sudan's war, humanitarian response, territorial changes, or all alleged violations.

explore_lenses.label: What changed on the ground in Oleshky?
explore_lenses.title: A limited corridor opened, not a wider truce
explore_lenses.summary: The operational change was a temporary, geographically limited pause in fighting that enabled aid deliveries and an evacuation route from occupied Oleshky; it did not stop combat elsewhere in the war.

claims.text: The ceasefire began simultaneously at 3:00 a.m. Kyiv time on October 27 and 4:00 a.m. Moscow time, according to Ukraine's human-rights ombudsman after contact with the Russian negotiating side.
Evacuees reached Ukrainian-held territory on October 31 after traveling by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus; aid groups were present to receive them at the Ukrainian-Belarusian border.
The truce was centered on Oleshky and nearby areas to permit humanitarian convoys, while Russian attacks continued elsewhere in Ukraine and Ukrainian drone attacks were reported in Russia.

explore_lenses.label: Why was an evacuation corridor needed?
explore_lenses.title: Entrapment, shortages and dangerous movement
explore_lenses.summary: The mission followed months of severe civilian constraints in a frontline occupied city, where access to food, health care and safe travel had sharply deteriorated.

claims.text: UN officials said that, as of early October, about 2,000 people, including 35 children, were reportedly trapped in Oleshky without food or medical supplies; drones and landmines had made routes unsafe and prevented organized evacuations.
UNHCR described Oleshky as a difficult frontline area with an estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people still present when the ceasefire began, and said the pause could allow aid and voluntary evacuation.

The United Nations said that it had not been formally asked to support this specific operation, although UNHCR supports Ukrainian authorities and partners with reception, accommodation, medical, legal and psychosocial assistance after evacuations.

Ukraine's Security Service says it has intelligence that Russian forces planned coercive or staged resident interviews concerning Oleshky; this is a Ukrainian government allegation, not independently verified in the cited notice.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after the localized truce?
explore_lenses.title: The immediate test is aid access and safe follow-up
explore_lenses.summary: The confirmed near-term task is to maintain safe humanitarian access through the truce's scheduled end and support evacuees; no extension or broader ceasefire has been publicly confirmed.

claims.text: AP reported that the localized ceasefire was scheduled to run until 10:59 p.m. local time on Sunday, November 1, while its precise geographic scope remained unclear.

Ukraine's ombudsman said on October 25 that arrangements were proceeding under a preliminary agreement and that work on the humanitarian mission would continue, but did not announce a subsequent evacuation timetable.

UNHCR said it hopes the ceasefire will bring relief and permit safe departures, and is prepared to support people once they are safely evacuated; this is an operational expectation rather than confirmation that further departures will occur.

AP reported that Russia, Ukraine and the United States were expected to hold trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next month to lay groundwork for detailed peace negotiations; this was separate from the Oleshky operation.

story_report.summary: Residents evacuated from Russia-occupied Oleshky reached Ukrainian-held territory on October 31 under a localized ceasefire brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. The evacuees traveled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus before aid groups received them at the Ukrainian-Belarusian border. Their arrival provided a route out of a frontline city where residents had been trapped amid dangerous conditions, though authorities withheld the number of people evacuated and the crossing location for security reasons.

sections.heading: Oleshky Residents Faced Severe Isolation
sections.body: U.N. officials said in early October that about 2,000 people, including 35 children, were reportedly trapped in Oleshky without food or medical supplies. UNHCR estimated that 1,700 to 2,000 people remained in the difficult frontline area when the ceasefire began. Drones and landmines had made routes unsafe and prevented organized evacuations, according to the United Nations.

sections.heading: Localized Truce Enabled Humanitarian Passage
sections.body: Ukraine’s human-rights ombudsman said the ceasefire began at 3 a.m. Kyiv time on October 27, simultaneously with 4 a.m. Moscow time, after contact with the Russian negotiating side. The truce was focused on Oleshky and nearby areas to allow humanitarian convoys, not a halt to the wider war: Russian attacks continued elsewhere in Ukraine and Ukrainian drone attacks were reported in Russia. AP reported the pause was scheduled to end at 10:59 p.m. local time on November 1, although its geographic scope was unclear.

sections.heading: Evacuation Support Remains Contingent
sections.body: The United Nations said it was not formally asked to support this operation, but UNHCR supports Ukrainian authorities and partners with reception, accommodation, medical, legal and psychosocial assistance after evacuations. UNHCR said it hoped the pause would permit safe departures and that it was prepared to assist people once evacuated. Those statements describe available support and expectations, rather than confirmation of further departures.

unresolved.text: Authorities have not publicly disclosed how many people were evacuated or the crossing point, citing the security of residents who remain in Oleshky and of future missions.
The conditions inside Oleshky and whether residents could freely make an informed choice of destination cannot be independently assessed from the available sources.
There is no confirmed public commitment to extend the local pause, evacuate all remaining residents, or turn the arrangement into a nationwide ceasefire.
